utterances.text: What is the principal mission of the 211th Brigade in the Malo Kosovo area?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The principal mission of the 211th Brigade in the Malo Kosovo area was to defend the state territory and to prepare to conduct combat operations against possible landing operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why against possible landing operations?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The area of Malo Kosovo is an area where a landing could easily take place. This is a good area for an enemy to stage a landing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just please clarify one thing for me. This is a dilemma that we encountered in a given testimony. Is there any distinction between parachute units and air-borne landing units?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, there is an important distinction between the two. The parachute units on the one hand and the air-borne landing units on the other. A parachute unit only has small arms. These units use parachutes to land. An air-borne landing unit is something that only major armies in the world have, such as NATO and Russia. Their one salient feature is this: In terms of weaponry these normally have heavy weapons and they use aeroplanes to get to an airport. Small parts of these units may use parachutes as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was the expression not used in a VJ document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just about to clarify the notion and the distinction between the two in relation to the 63rd Parachute Brigade. That would be my next question. [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, the 63rd Parachute Brigade, what sort of brigade was that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: It was a parachute brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did the VJ have an air-borne landing brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about the 63rd, did it have any armoured vehicles or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No. The 63rd Parachute Brigade had all the distinctive features of a parachute brigade, they only had small arms and light vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. Now we're about to move on to a different topic. Who was your nearest neighbour, speaking of VJ forces, obviously, which brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: My nearest neighbour was the 354th Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's see a document they produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5D499, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm afraid there is a mistranslation in this document. Item 3 in the English, it appears that a portion is simply not there, a portion of the Serbian original. Therefore, we could read it out and then we could mark it for retranslation, by your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, it seems that we have a translation problem there. Please, the last paragraph under item 3, it starts with the following words: "In Podujevo municipal territory ..." If you see that, item 3, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: "In Podujevo municipal territory by 1800 hours about 15.000 refugees (returnees) of Albanian ethnicity had arrived who were put up in Ladovac village and Sajkovac village."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall duly be submitted this document for retranslation in order to deal with this error.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, were you aware of this situation?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, we were neighbouring units and I was aware of this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were some of these villages in or near your own sector, Ladovac, Sajkovac?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, near my sector, Sajkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you put up these refugees? Did you assist them?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's in the statement, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. [Interpretation] There is a document that I would like to see that is not in the statement, 5D615.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you direct us to the paragraph of the statement that deals with this, please. If it's not there then proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm afraid the document before us is not the right one. I asked for 5D615. Colonel, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I do. This is a combat report by the command of the 211th Armoured Brigade. The date is the 26th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: At item 5.2(B) you talk about the behaviour of the police and you say they seem not to have been clear about the fact that they have been resubordinated to the brigade commander. Why did you state that and what was this about really?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: There had been an order by the Pristina Corps command pursuant to which it was necessary by the 25th of April to have MUP units resubordinated to the Pristina Corps, or rather, to the VJ. Given the fact that this had in fact not been done by the 25th, I believed it was necessary to inform the commander of the Pristina Corps about this. MUP officers got in touch with me to tell me that they had received no such order to be resubordinated to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. Did this resubordination occur later on?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for the sake of time I have one or two more questions left and a document that I will be tendering later on. This is 5D1070 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... circumstances. You ought to be exercising greater discretion by this stage in -- if you want to present any other witnesses to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave just last and final question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Same document, second page I need.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, item 9, requests. We see what it says, a request for humanitarian aid in terms of food primarily. Can you tell me what this is about?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Given the fact that food had run out for the Siptar population, I deemed it necessary to inform my superior in order for him to get in touch with the district -- provincial Executive Council to put in an intervention so that assistance might be provided to those people in terms of food supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And the last thing, paragraph 21 of your statement you describe that members of your unit assisted a sick Albanian whom they drove to Pristina under difficult conditions, difficult circumstances. What was the name of the medical officer, the doctor, who assisted this person?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: It was a doctor from my own unit, Lazarov.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I have several questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P626 brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, are you familiar with this document? If you would like that, I have a hard copy to show you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, no, I am familiar with this document. This is a reminder for Yugoslav Army members engaged in areas affected by sabotage and terrorist activities. It was issued by the VJ General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Throughout 1999 were you, your unit, and members of your unit acting in accordance with this reminder?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: This was one of the responsibilities for every member of the 211th Armoured Brigade, a responsibility of being familiar with this reminder for VJ members and another responsibility was to act in compliance with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Just in order to save time, let me put it this way. Let's not take this paragraph by paragraph. Would I be right in saying that this reminder contains specific instructions on how to treat captured terrorists, how to treat those sick and wounded, terrorists as well as civilians, how to approach issues regarding property, that sort of thing; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, you're entirely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, counsel for Sreten Lukic, and I will also have some questions to put to you today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all I would request Exhibit 5D1329 in e-court, and I believe once this comes up, we will see this is the map that was prepared for the legitimate anti-terrorist action Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There we have it. And, sir, looking at this document, first of all, do you recognise it as a map that either you drew or that you authorised to be drawn insofar as the -- as far as your name is in the bottom right-hand corner of the same?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision map produced by the commander of the 211th Armoured Brigade to block, crush, and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the Bajgora area or sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say it was produced by the commander of the 211th Armoured Brigade, did you personally draft this map or did someone else do it at your behest?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: This was done by the command of the 211th Armoured Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know when precisely this map was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: This map was drafted sometime in the second half of April 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you have an explanation for the fact that this map in front of us is not signed?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I assume that this is the second copy of the original map, and the original map is probably still kept in the archives of the brigade. Could we just lower the map slightly, pull it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could move the map slightly down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other way around, please. Right. You see where it says: "I hereby approve, Commander Vladimir Lazarevic," and above that it says: "Keep permanently."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you expect that the copy number would be filled in on the right-hand side where it says, I believe "prilog" or it -- where it has the space that says [B/C/S spoken] and then it has a space that has not been filled in. If this was the copy for the archives would you expect there to be a notation there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: There should be one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, upon what basis were you able to draw the positions and tasks of the various PJP that are depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I had received an order from the Pristina Corps commander and a decision map from the Pristina Corps commander with the axes of operations of the PJP drawn in. I copied those axes onto my own map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I see on this map from your command the abbreviation "SAJ," what does that mean on this map and where did you get that information from?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: As I said a while ago, I copied the PJP axes from the decision map of the Pristina Corps commander. "SAJ" means special anti-terrorist units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you Exhibit P1975, and if I could have the usher's assistance I'd like to hand you a hard copy, since I don't intend to go through every step of this document; but I do want you to have the opportunity to do so if required. And once you receive this document the first question I wanted to ask you: Is this the order that you mentioned that you received from the Pristina Corps's commander along with a decision map?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is the order to crush and destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the Bajgora-Bare area and I received this from the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now you can feel free to look through the document and in particular the section entitled: "Assignments," but my question for you is: Would you agree with me that this document, the written order for this action, does not explicitly name either the SAJ or the PJP units to be involved in this action?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No. That was shown on the map and that is why I included that in my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I correct that this action was undertaken by all the units depicted on the map in the manner depicted on the map?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, generally speaking would you agree with me that forces engaged in a line of blockade must maintain either visual line of sight or line of fire coverage with themselves in order to successfully prevent spillover of enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by visual line of sight or by line of fire coverage for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask it a different way. Would you agree with me that the distance or separation between units engaged in a blockade has to be such so as to permit them to have visual line of sight with one another or to be able to cover that gap between the forces with fire, if need be, to prevent the spillover of enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I don't understand. Who is it that's supposed to be able to see one another?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With -- well, let's return to 5D1329 the map for a second maybe I could short-circuit this by showing on the map what I'm referring to, and if we can look at the bottom section of the map, it's around the area of Vucitrn; but I don't know if it could be visible with this type of map, it's the area of deployment of the 15th Armoured Brigade, as depicted here. You'll bear with me, sir, while we wait for the map to come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If it can help I could put up a copy on the ELMO since the point I'm making is very -- there we are. Now we have it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we see in the area -- in the line of deployment of the 15th Armoured Brigade several sets of -- of red lines indicating the line of blockade. Would you agree with me that the distance between the red lines denoting position of forces had to be such so that they could visually see that area in between and be able to cover it with fire, if need be, if enemy forces tried to pass through that gap? And I'm talking about that area where there's a sizeable gap just above 15 OKBR that exists on this version of the map.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I think I understand. You mean there should be a line of sight between the two red lines that are marked here and there is some distance between the two. Not necessarily. Not necessarily at all times. They can use signals equipment to communicate, the two units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now would you agree with me that in order to successfully blockade and prevent spillover of terrorists or enemy forces, those units would have to see anyone trying to breakthrough that gap and be able to cover that area with fire, if need be?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, fire and movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, having that in mind, does this depiction of the line of blockade comport with that principle and does it comport with your recollections of the position of forces for this action? That is to say: Is the gap here too big?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I wasn't in the area myself, and I'm not familiar with the area. I know the area that is to the south-east [as interpreted] of these lines, where the 211th Armoured Brigade actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you recall if the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a correction for the transcript. When the witness was explaining about what he knew and what he saw, page 57, line 16, he said north-east not south-east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Having in mind the question that was raised of whether this is actually the map from the archive or not, do you recall if the map that you drafted had this large gap in the line of blockade, the map that you drafted at the time of the action?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: This is the map. At the outset I said that these lines to the south-west, the lines of the armoured brigade, were crossed out, or rather, were copied from the decision of the Pristina Corps commander because I didn't know exactly where the positions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we can move on to another action, 5D1070 is the next exhibit I wish to have you look at. And when this comes up can you first, sir, confirm for me whether, in fact, this is a document originating from your brigade signed by you on the second page, which we could have shown to you if need be.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is a combat report of the 211th Armoured Brigade dated the 25th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we could stay on the first page of this document we see section 2.1 of this combat report, and could you for us -- I don't know whether we have a translation. Could we have you, for the sake of time, read out the first sentence of 2.1 and tell me if you recall this particular anti-terrorist action. Again, sir, can we have you read it out loud and tell us if you recall this action, as I ought not to be translating the document for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: "The units of the brigade were focusing on supporting forces of the MUP and the SAJ in crushing and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the broader area of the village of Palatna and with part of their forces, they were carrying out a blockade of the Siptar terrorist forces and preventing withdrawals in the territory of Bajgora and Malo Kosovo. The construction of the road between the village of Rekalija and the village of Kodralija, combat control of the territory and taking measures of anti-aircraft -- of air defence and anti-aircraft defence." Should I go on reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you recall what action this is referring to, what anti-terrorist action this is referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Units of the brigade were engaged in crushing and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the broader area of the village of Palatna to -- with a smaller part of the forces that were carrying out a blockade and preventing withdrawal of the Siptar terrorist forces from the territory of Bajgora towards Malo Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for clarity there's a second sentence. Could you read that aloud for us and let me know whether that, in fact, refers to the same combat action or is it a different combat action?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: "Part of the command organs headed by the commander and the Chief of Staff participate in carrying out combat operations and the rest are engaged in providing assistance to units in the sectors of deployment." Yes. That pertains to that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And lastly on this document if you look at item number 4, subsection (A). Can you read for us the subsection (A) and tell us whether, in fact, this is still the same combat action, and then I will move on to another document relating to the same.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: "Positive effect on morale. Properly carried out scientific, technical, and moral psychological preparations for carrying out the task of cleaning up the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Palatna. Direct command over the action by the commander and the Chief of Staff." Yes, that pertains to that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to refer to Exhibit 6D709 in e-court, and for your purposes if I could again give you a hard copy, it might be easier since it's a multi-page document to move through this quicker since I have very few questions about this document. This appears to be an order of the command of the Pristina Corps dated May 22nd, 1999, strictly confidential 455-253 for crushing and eliminating the STS in the region of Palatna. Can you confirm whether, in fact, this order is for the action that we just saw the last document reporting the undertaking of in the region of Palatna village. And if you need to find the assignments for your brigade, I believe it's section 5.1, the bottom of the second page in Serbian, the top of the third page in English, if that assists you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, these are not the same actions. This action is carried out a month after the one that you showed me a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, how do you account for the date being the 22nd of May of this document and the document we just looked at being the 25th of May? How can there be a -- how can this action be occurring a month after the combat report that's dated three days later?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The first action was being carried out at the same time when the blockade was being carried out in relation to Bajgora, exception that it went in a different direction. Not all forces were engaged in the blockade. A part of the 2nd Mechanised Battalion was acting towards Palatna simultaneously with the blockade, that is to say towards Bajgora, whereas this is a completely different action a month later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're saying that the report that we've just seen was a report relating to events a month before it was written?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The report was the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, it's the 25th of May, unless it's a misprint.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could assist, I could hand a hard copy of that document since we can't have two documents up in e-court, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That way we can clear that up. I apologise, my copy is marked with the sections he's just read. I hope that doesn't cause any problems for Mr. Stamp. He's able to look at it, if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Looking at the prior document, 5D, I believe it was, 170 [sic], does that refresh your recollection that that document was dated the 25th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 1070, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the 25th of May, 1999. That is to say that this is a report pertaining to the action towards Palatna.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does this combat report cover the action that is described in Exhibit 6D709 which you also have in front of you, the "zapovest," order, for Palatna -- the region of Palatna I should say?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we could turn to item number 14 of the "zapovest," order, 6D709, that's the -- item 14 is on the last page just before the signature, and you will see here it is referenced that the command of the 211th Brigade is to lead the planning, organization, and implementation of the combat operations. Would you agree that this was the case in this action?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. It pertained to the 211th Armoured Brigade and the 354th Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And had there been any problems encountered in fulfilling this or any other direct order contained in this document in the implementation of the combat operation that would be reported in your combat report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now while I agree that the VJ and MUP officers each commanded their own contingents during the course of the action, isn't it correct that for this anti-terrorist action your command led, organized, and took charge of the planning and organization for this action?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I've already said that I was in charge of planning and leading the action of the 211th Armoured Brigade and the 354th Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, would you find a suitable place to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think we should probably do it now since the next paragraph I want to go to would require some time and I could -- if I can find the B/C/S I can cut that down because I think there's a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These matters we've dealt with so far are all matters that were not dealt with in the statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe, apart from the -- the part about Bajgora, that might have been mentioned in one of the paragraphs, but I could be mistaken since with the pace we've been working at I had to prepare most of these questions before having this statement -- the final statement to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gergar, we require to have a break at this stage. While we have that break could you leave the courtroom, please, with the usher and we will see you again at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you again, Colonel Gergar. If I could ask you -- well, I think I can clear up this question that I was asking you with respect to the Palatna action by looking at another action in the Malo Kosovo region that you discuss at paragraph 32 of your written statement. Now, I'm going to have to ask for a certain portion of that paragraph to be written -- to be read into the record, as the official English translation on the face of it gives -- has an imprecise translation exactly on the part that I want to ask. So I'm going to ask once this comes up, sir, you'll see in the middle of paragraph 32 the part -- I guess I better wait for it to come up on the screen otherwise it will be more difficult. That's 5D1400, I believe. It should be approximately page 7 of the English, and in the -- in the B/C/S something just happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's already on the screen so you could proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in the middle of paragraph 32 of your statement there is a section that begins: "The action lasted one day and took place in cooperation with MUP forces on 24 March 1999." Are you able to find that section of paragraph 32?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you then for the record read for us the remainder of paragraph 32 as it is written in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I can. "During the action, a group of officers from the command of the Pristina Corps commanded the action from the Laus feature where their command post was located, namely, at the command post of the 354th Brigade. As far as I can recall, it was Colonel Nikolic, Major Djordjevic, and two other officers whose names I cannot remember, and they led the action of the VJ forces while MUP officers commanded their contingents."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this action --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you move on let the record reflect that that's exactly the translation which is in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct. In the English translation of the statement, and we have the same word being translated -- we have two different words being translated into the same word in English. I think I'm going to have to address that to CLSS. I don't know how else to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What are you talking about, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Komandovati" and "rukovoditi" is being translated as "commanded" in both instances in the English and in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's wrong with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They are two entirely different terms with different meanings attached. They are very precise terms that have meanings in both the police and in the military terminology, Your Honours; and it makes a difference as to who commanded -- well let me ask the question to the witness because by talking about it this way I might actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where are the words used or where are the different words set out in that passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In that passage it says that in -- when it talks about the command group from the Pristina Corps "rukovodjenje aksija" [Interpretation] Exercised control over the action. [In English] And then the bottom the last part of it the word "komandovanje" is being translated the same as "rukovodjenje."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you want it to be different, do you, because the other meaning that has just been given suggested I would have thought suggested that the VJ had some superior position, whereas the translation as it is makes it clear that the VJ and MUP forces were separately commanded. Now, do you want it to be different from that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want it to be what the document is, Your Honour. I don't want it to be anything apart from what the document says and does in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you want instead of commanded the action from the Laus feature were in control of the action. That's what you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Manage would be better or led, I think is the -- is the -- except the term for "rukovodjenje" that we had even just prior to the break in one of the other answers by the witness use the term "rukovodjenje"; and it was translated as led. So I really don't know what the status is of that word is as far as the translation is concerned. I don't know how to ask questions when the words are translated differently every chance. They're terms of art that have a specific meaning and that's where we get confused as counsel and where witnesses get confused where these words get interpreted as being either the same or being different when in Serbian they have a certain meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have to say I'm finding it difficult to see what the point of your position is but please continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree with me that while the formation commanders or formation superior officers of both the MUP and the VJ units that were involved in this particular action passed orders down to their forces and therefore commanded their forces in the course of the action, that this action was being led by the VJ officers that you name here from the Pristina Corps command, that they, if I can turn to Serbian [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. At the Laus feature there was a group of officers from the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, there was no question picked up there because he was speaking over the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I just say, I am not sure what exactly the witness could be saying yes to in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't worry, Mr. Stamp, that's exactly my problem, so I have no idea what this means at the moment. The idea of leading seems to be something different from commanding, and perhaps the witness is going to explain that in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you in your own mind as a professional VJ officer differentiate between commanders commanding their units and commanders leading or "rukovodjenje aksija"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well can we have that in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Lead, exercise control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the next word was important as well, there was more than one word there, and the other one, I think, was action.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand it properly either. I think it was action too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, in English, please, either that or all in Serb and we'll get it translated, but this does not work speaking in two languages at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know how else to do it apart from going all Serbian then I guess for this particular question if that's all right with, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gergar, Mr. Ivetic doesn't seem to be able to do this. What's the difference between what is said at the beginning of the passage you read that's what the group of officers were doing and commanding? What's the difference between these two things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, in our terminology commanders command. That is to say higher organs can lead or effect control, exercise control. Immediate command is carried out by commanders. In this case, the group of officers that had come from the command of the Pristina Corps led this action, whereas the commander, Lazarevic, would command me in that action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you see, I have great difficulty with that because the first sentence says that the group of officers led the action, and then it identifies the same officers as commanding the VJ forces, not a different officer called Lazarevic. So I don't understand your explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I receive commands from my superior, and the group of officers had the role of coordinators. I sent reports to them and they coordinated, coordinated action with the other units. Once I report to General Lazarevic, then he issues a commanding order to me as to what it is that I should do after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- I think we're -- that's all I'm going to get out of him for that section. I think the paragraph does explain that the action was undertaken so I don't have to ask questions about that. If we can move on then to Exhibit 5D595, and again if first you can confirm that this is a document originating from your command dated the 9th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order by the command of the 211th Armoured Brigade, the date is the 9th of May, 1999. This is about supplementing the defence system or upgrading the defence system.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn to the second page in the B/C/S or Serbian I should say, item 10, and it's on the second page of the English also item 10, I won't read this section, sir; but it seems here that you are giving assignments to your subordinates to protect population and their property from various bad things. Did you, in fact, during the entire course of the war undertake measures to protect the civilian population and their property from theft, looting, arson, et cetera? And if you know, did other VJ formations in your or near your region undertake the same responsibilities within their zones?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout the war, in my zone of responsibility I was responsibility for maintaining order and discipline. My order clearly states that all my subordinate commands had the same responsibility as well as any other commands that were near me in my immediate vicinity that were supposed to take measures to prevent indiscipline, theft, and other occurrences of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's all I have for that document. If we could now move to 5D591, and if we look at -- that's a one-page document. First off, do you recall in item 2 you mention that volunteers are to be sent to the school Aca Marovic in Kosovo Polje. Do you recall that there was a subcentre, a reception subcentre for volunteers in Kosovo Polje of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, it was based on an order from the Pristina Corps command that I learned that volunteers were to be admitted and dispatched to Kosovo Polje in order to perform further duties with them and assign them to units of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, these specific volunteers that you're talking about within your zone, where did these volunteers come from? Could someone just show up at the border and express an intention to volunteer?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Someone could simply show up and express an intention or a desire to volunteer in the units of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now turning to another topic. Do you recall what Ministry of the Interior forces were in the second half of April 1999 within your zone of responsibility and that of the 354th Infantry Brigade that you have also testified about here today?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Within the zone of responsibility of the 211th Armoured Brigade, there were MUP forces, meaning PJP forces, and the Podujevo Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which PJP forces were in your zone and within the zone of the 354th Brigade, infantry brigade, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I think it was the 122nd Detachment of the PJP or possibly the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my colleague Mr. Cepic showed you one of your reports where you talked about the MUP units not knowing that they were supposed to be resubordinated to you. I'd like to show you a document, 6D1023, which is attachment number 2 to a plan -- or, excuse me, an order of the Pristina Corps dated the 25th of April, 1999, that we've had in evidence prior regarding engagement of MUP forces. First of all, sir, do you recall receiving such a plan for engagement of combined forces as an attachment to an order from the Pristina Corps? And perhaps if we can turn to the second page. I believe that the second page in both versions covers your unit in item 10.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I don't remember this plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to asking you the following question let me just call up briefly P2809, a Prosecution exhibit that is the first part of this document. Do you recall receiving this order from your superior command on or about the 25th of April, 1999? And if need be, we can go to the last page of the document if it would help you, sir, if this doesn't refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, I don't recall this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you see in item number 2 of this document that attachment or appendix to, as it's translated in the English, is said to be a plan of engagement of combined contingents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the witness said he doesn't recall this document. Secondly, I find it very difficult for the witness to be expected to identify the relevant portion in English since Mr. Gergar does not, in fact, understand or speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I thought that in asking questions in English I have to use the official English translation of the Serbian document which is side by side with the official English translation. If the official translation is wrong, Mr. Cepic can say it's wrong, I actually don't believe it is in this instance but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The real point here is the witness says he doesn't know anything about this. What is it you're now trying to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if we can go to the last page, I think we'll see that it was directed to his brigade, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right, go to the last page then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at the bottom left, it is the customary and procedure of the Army of Yugoslavia to list recipients on the bottom left of every document sent from a superior command to subordinates?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there an answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please hear the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I wonder if we need the question, in fact, Mr. Ivetic. We've had it from umpteen people already.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you see here, sir, where the document says it was sent to all subordinate commands?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As of the 25th of April, 1999, weren't you, in fact, a subordinate command of the Pristina Corps that would have received this order from your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I was a subordinate command, but I don't remember receiving a document like this. It has been nine years, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That part I understand. Now, if we can turn back to the first page of this document, I will continue with a line of questioning I had about appendix 2. Having in regard what is stated in paragraph 2 of this order from the Pristina Corps command - and let me know when you've -- when you've -- when you've read that section to yourself, just paragraph 2 now ...

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I've read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Keeping that in mind if we can turn to 6D1023 and look at the title of this document, do you accept the very strong likelihood that this document is, in fact, the appendix to -- that was referenced in the prior order, indeed having the same title, date, and source of origin?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: It's possible that this plan of engagement was an appendix to the document that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we could turn to the second page of this document in both the Serbian and the English, and if I can direct your attention to paragraph 10 of this plan of engagement. And if I can direct your attention to the -- well, I guess it would be the fourth -- the fourth column, if we include the one column that has the numbers. Does that reflect the actual forces of the MUP that were within your zone of responsibility as you recollect them? The -- I should say the PJP units of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now if you look at line 12 of this plan, I believe it relates to the 354th Infantry Brigade that you identified as a neighbouring force, and if you look at that same column under the 354th will you agree with me that the exact same MUP PJP units are slated to be resubordinated to the 354th Brigade that were supposed to be resubordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, they're the same, the same forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Having in mind that you do not recall this --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see my colleague's on my [sic] feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the witness clearly said he didn't remember this, and now he's being pushed to speculate. We're wasting precious time. My other witnesses are waiting. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, he's simply being asked to confirm on the face of the document the same units appear in two separate parts associated with two separate VJ units, and that's -- he's done no more than that. He's not confirmed a personal recollection that that was so. So please continue, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Having in mind, sir, that you do not recall this particular plan of engagement and having in mind your combat report complaining about confusion of the PJP in terms of who they were supposed to be resubordinated to, do you accept now the possibility that, in fact, some of the confusion was caused by the fact that they were receiving requests for resubordination from two brigades in the same area?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No. I was told by officers from the PJP that they had received no order to resubordinate themselves to the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to resubordination, is your understanding of the word include the fact that they were supposed to become an essential part of your brigade even outside of combat actions?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I can move on now. If we can -- if we can focus on your brigade for a second, am I correct that the numerical strength of your brigade in April -- strike that. Just, can you tell us what the numerical strength of your brigade is, including the breakdown between active servicemen and reservists?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, did it change from when the bombing started to the end of the war? Did it fluctuate much? I mean, I want the time-period of the war with NATO and the STS from March 24th, 1999, onwards.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: From the beginning of the war the numerical strength of the brigade was about 2.200 up to 2.300 men. There were about 1.000 reservists among those men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did the strength of your brigade increase during the war; and if so, what was the largest -- the most that it attained and again what portion of that was reservists and what portion were active servicemen?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I said the strength was about 2.200 to 2.300 men, and it didn't change to any significant extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what about the numerical strength of the 94th Military Territorial Detachment that was supposed to have been resubordinated to your brigade on the 24th of April, 1999, what was its strength?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The 94th Military Territorial Detachment, I'm not familiar with that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can -- one moment, please. Now, let me move on and I'll see if I need that. You mentioned the 354th Infantry Brigade. Am I correct or am I close in stating that they had approximately 5.795 members, of whom 5.600 were reservists in the time-period between the beginning of the war through April the 18th, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I don't know what their strength was precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does the figure I've quoted seem reasonable based upon your knowledge and recollections or if not -- if you have another figure, I would be more than happy to hear it.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Well, I said I really don't know what its numerical strength was, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Can you concede that they were almost entirely reservists?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes. The majority of that brigade was reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel, for your time, and I apologise for any confusion relating from translation issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gergar, you'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good day, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just by way of background, can you tell me were you in 19 -- or in 2001 indicted for negligence in respect to the death of one of your soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, a criminal complaint was filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What happened to that case? What was the result?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: It was thrown out as unfounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To move on, is it correct that your unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I would like the exact interpretation of what the witness said to be entered, if I may quote what I repeat he says: "The criminal complaint was thrown out as unfounded," so what was thrown out. We need to know that, don't we. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's already clear from the transcript that that's what was thrown out, and you've taken it beyond any doubt. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us today that the brigade -- the 211th Brigade was resubordinated to the Pristina Corps on the 29th of March, 1999. Now, prior to that were units from that brigade not brought into the area of responsibility of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, the units had been brought earlier to the zone of responsibility of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is -- and when these units were brought there, were they not resubordinated to the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, but the name was different, not the 211th Armoured Brigade, but rather Tactical Group 211.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that was comprised of -- among other units, it was comprised of a mechanised battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if the transfer, relocation, of that unit into Kosovo into the area of responsibility of the Pristina Corps was reported to the KVM monitors who were there at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you have any sort of association or correspondence with any of the KVM monitors?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that answer refer to the whole period up until June? Oh, in fact -- sorry, my mistake. Does it apply to the whole period up until March the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yeah, thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Weren't these -- well, were you aware that bringing in these units would be in breach of the undertakings made by the FRY in October of 1998 in regard to movement of VJ units?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was the movement of the units of the brigade into Kosovo in early March or on the 15th of March, 1999, done in secret, that is, in a manner to avoid observation by the OSCE observers?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. But you were aware, sir, that the movement of that unit into Kosovo constituted a build-up of VJ forces from outside Kosovo into Kosovo in early May -- sorry, early March 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you aware of other units that had been brought into Kosovo from outside of Kosovo before the NATO intervention?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you arrived in Kosovo, I think your statement says that you were mostly involved combat training. Apart from combat training were you involved in any other activity like combat?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: You mean up until the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Between the time you arrived up until when the war began.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The unit was staying at the training-grounds Batlava, and it was not engaged in any other combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think in your statement you said that -- or tell me, when you arrived in March 1999 were there not KLA positions near to where you became based?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: They were not in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, how far were the nearest KLA units?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Over 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you engage any of those units or have any contact with any of those units before the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to the action of the -- that began on the 25th or 26th of April. But first I'd like to ask you some questions about the map that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but I see here in the transcript that it says "April"; however, what we heard in the B/C/S interpretation was "October." So I would kindly ask my colleague Mr. Stamp to repeat the question. I think that would be best because we got a completely wrong interpretation into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He's going off to deal with something else, and no doubt we'll deal with the date when he comes back to this. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said in respect to the map that you drew that perhaps the reason it was not signed is because it was a second copy. How many maps were prepared by you or by your command? And when I say "maps," how many of these maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we put the map before him, 5D1329.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The thing is I just want to know how many of these maps are prepared by your brigade command. I shouldn't say "these." This particular map. How many of this particular map you see before you was prepared by your brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: This decision map was done in two copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, was any of those two copies signed?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, the original was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you recall if you actually saw that signed copy?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I certainly saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that would have been -- tell me if this procedure is right. That would have been signed by you, sent off to General Lazarevic, who also signed it, so it would be signed twice?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is to say my decision map is signed by myself, that is obligatory, and then I take that decision map to the corps commander for his approval and he signs it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is it dated at any of those signings?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, what -- it is a signed original that is archived?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The original should be arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the other copy, where is that kept?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: One copy is given to the corps command, and we keep the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I take it that your understanding is that this map you see in front of you is a copy that was kept by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not clear now, Mr. Stamp, whether there is an original and two copies; or whether there are two maps, one of which is an original.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sir, I -- well, I'm going to ask you this. This map that you see in front of you, there were two copies prepared, an original and a copy; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know where your brigade records were stored after the war?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I think in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which archives?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were kept in the archives of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Just to get my bearings on this -- or all bearings on this map. Is -- or does this map cover the area that includes the town of Vucitrn?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I really cannot see because it's rather illegible, it's pretty small, fine print. Could it please be enlarged a bit? It is very hard to read what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But would you be able to identify where major population centres are like Vucitrn and Podujevo just by looking at the deployment of forces on these maps? Don't you know where the forces were deployed in relation to these population centres?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: No, I was never in Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do the green arrows represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the axes of activity of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, now, and what do the blue markings represent?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: The blue markings are the enemy forces, the terrorists in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now you -- I think you said that you had -- there was a support artillery unit -- sorry, there was mortar, you had mortar units that were engaged. Where were your mortar units located?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: In this period the mortar company was in the area of Bajcina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you see that area on the map as it is there now?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GERGAR
utterances.text: I can really barely see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, would you find a suitable point to interrupt. If you need a few more questions to deal finally with the map, that's fine; but if you're going to be some time, we should just break off now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think this might be a convenient moment because I might ask him to mark something and that might take some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Gergar, we must conclude our proceedings for the day at this stage; that means you need to return to complete your evidence. Meanwhile, overnight it is a strict rule that you have no communication with anybody at all, anybody at all, about the evidence. You can talk to whoever you like about other things, but to no one at all about any part of the evidence. Now could you leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you tomorrow morning at 9.00 in Courtroom I.
